subject: Re: Discrepancy between AWS Marketplace invoice and internal meter ledger — VAT implications
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-11-22 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: AWS Marketplace invoice shows additional 12,340 USD for 'redwood-prod' — need breakdown and VAT evidence

Hi Mina,

We received the November AWS Marketplace invoice (attached) and it includes an extra charge of 12,340.00 USD under the SKU redwood-prod-usage that doesn't match our daily meter exports. Our procurement team flagged that the invoice line has VAT applied at 20% and we need the underlying usage granularity (meter IDs and timestamps) to reconcile and decide whether we can reclaim VAT in our EU entity.

Can your team provide:
- A per-meter breakdown (meter ID, start/end timestamp, token/units billed) for account mpacct-987654
- Any mapping to our internal project tags (we think it should be project:acme-logistics-prod)
- Explanation for the currency conversion (invoice is USD, our ledger is EUR)

Samantha (cc: Procurement), we need this by EOD Monday as they are pushing the payment cutoff.

Thanks,
Samantha Green
Finance Manager — Acme Logistics
Attachments: aws-invoice-202611.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22 11:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoice shows additional 12,340 USD for 'redwood-prod' — need breakdown and VAT evidence

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the attachment.

We pulled the initial ledger and it looks like there are three potential causes: a) a late-batched billing window on 2026-11-16 that included prefixed KV cache charges, b) a cross-entity meter attribution where some usage was billed to the Marketplace account instead of your project account, and c) a USD/EUR FX rounding delta from the Marketplace aggregator.

I'm looping in Jonas (billing ops) and Vanessa (account lead) to provide the per-meter CSV and to confirm attribution. Ben, can you validate whether the VAT treatment on AWS side follows the seller's EU registration? If not, we may need to issue a credit memo and provide VAT evidence for Acme to reclaim.

We will provide:
- Per-meter export (meter ID, start/end, units, model, route) — ETA 24 hours
- A short reconciliation mapping to your project tags — ETA 36 hours
- Draft credit memo if we confirm overbilling — ETA 48 hours

If Procurement needs an interim note to delay the payment cutoff, let us know and we can provide a short statement.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Finance Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme-usage-202611-meters.csv (pending)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23 07:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoice shows additional 12,340 USD for 'redwood-prod' — need breakdown and VAT evidence

Hi all,

Attached is the per-meter export for account mpacct-987654 (CSV). Key findings from a quick pass:
- Metered lines 2026-11-16 22:00–23:59 (UTC) include three batched entries labeled prefix-cache-KV that were applied to the marketplace seller account rather than the linked project account. Total of those lines = 9,860.00 USD.
- An FX revaluation line applied on 2026-11-18 shows a rounding loss of 1,120.00 USD due to AWS aggregate conversion from EUR->USD on their settlement date.
- Remaining delta (1,360.00 USD) appears to be for a one-off burst on 2026-11-20 that our routing policy routed to the marketplace seller pool during a capacity overflow.

CSV columns: meter_id, start_utc, end_utc, units, sku, billed_usd, seller_account, project_tag
Sample rows included.

Next steps:
- Vanessa will confirm project_tag mappings for Acme (we think project:acme-logistics-prod maps to tag acme-prod-42).
- Ben to confirm VAT registration status for our seller account in the EU and whether AWS applied VAT at collection.
- Mina will prepare a draft credit memo for the 9,860 USD misattribution and propose retention for the FX 1,120 USD as a separate adjustment.

Jonas
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme-usage-202611-meters.csv
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme-corp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoice shows additional 12,340 USD for 'redwood-prod' — need breakdown and VAT evidence

Thanks Jonas — that helps a lot. A couple quick items from Procurement:
- They need a concise statement we can hand to our tax advisor confirming the 9,860 USD was billed to the marketplace seller account in error and will be credited by Redwood. A signed PDF is ideal.
- For the FX rounding, our treasury team needs the AWS settlement timestamp and the conversion rate used so they can determine whether the VAT base was impacted. Can you pull the AWS settlement record?
- For the one-off burst (1,360 USD), can you confirm whether there was an autoscaling event tied to their production traffic that caused the fallback routing? If so, we need timestamps and route IDs.

Procurement is willing to extend the payment cutoff by 48 hours if we can provide the signed statement and draft credit memo within that window.

Samantha
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24 14:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoice shows additional 12,340 USD for 'redwood-prod' — need breakdown and VAT evidence

Samantha — summary and next steps below. We will provide the signed statement and draft credit memo by EOD today per your cutoff extension.

Summary findings (from our ledger + AWS settlement pull):
- Misattribution credit: 9,860.00 USD — caused by a late-batched KV/prefix cache billing window (meter IDs start: MTR-20261116-00 through MTR-20261116-27). We will issue a credit memo for the full amount; draft attached.
- FX rounding delta: 1,120.00 USD — AWS settlement timestamp: 2026-11-18T03:12:22Z; conversion rate used by AWS: 1 EUR = 1.0664 USD (settlement note attached). We will provide the settlement record in a format acceptable to your treasury/tax advisor.
- Fallback burst: 1,360.00 USD — occurred 2026-11-20 18:14:00Z to 18:27:00Z; routed to seller pool via route-id RTE-RED-POOL-77 during a transient capacity overflow. This routing was policy-compliant but we will include the route trace.

Deliverables attached:
1) Signed statement (short PDF) confirming the 9,860 USD misattribution and commitment to credit.
2) Draft credit memo (credit-memo-draft-ACME-202611.pdf).
3) AWS settlement extract (CSV) with timestamp and conversion rate.
4) Meter-level CSV (acme-usage-202611-meters.csv).

Vanessa, Ben — please confirm you approve the signed statement and credit memo for issuance. Monica, finance ops will prepare the final credit memo entry and confirm the posting date (we propose 2026-11-24 so Acme can clear the payment once credit posts).

If Procurement still needs anything else to finalize payment delay, let us know.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Finance Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Attachments: credit-memo-draft-ACME-202611.pdf, acme-usage-202611-meters.csv, aws-settlement-20261118.csv, signed-statement-acme-202611.pdf
